To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the gas from minor coal seams, which may be interbedded with shale with no gas, contributes significantly to the production from a coal seam, with the gas from the shale exceeding that of the coal after ~8 years of production.
the inclusion of minor coal seams and shale beds with gas in lateral wells results in more producible gas and water than if the main coal seam was the only reservoir considered.
the contribution of gas in minor coal seams and adjacent shale beds to gas production in a lateral is significant and should be included in the production model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the contribution to production from minor coals seams and adjacent shales in a lateral drilled in the Mannville coal seam in south central Alberta, Canada.
understanding the production of gas from the coal and shale reservoirs in the Mannville producing region of south central Alberta.
the contribution to gas production from the minor coal seam and the interbedded shaly units in the Mannville producing interval.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
gas from coal seams and gas shale beds should be considered as a resource in any coal bed methane development.
the contribution of gas from adjacent minor coal seams and shales should be included in the production forecast and economic evaluation of coalbed gas reservoirs.
the gas stored in minor coal seams and in the interbedded shaly gas reservoirs adjacent to the main Mannville producing coal seams should be considered when developing the reservoir.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, when drilling a lateral wellbore in a main coal seam, the production from the minor coal beds and interbedded shaley gas reservoirs is significant, and should be included in reservoir modelling studies to optimize development of the producing fairway.
the gas stored in the minor coals and interbedded shale gas beds is a potential source of additional gas that could be recovered in a producing fairway.

the inclusion of minor coals and gas shales adjacent to the main Mannville seam results in 1) 1.7 times more gas and 2) 2.5 times more water produced after 25 years than when the main Mannville Seam is considered alone.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the gas in the coal and adjacent shale beds should not be overlooked.
the production from the minor coal and shale beds is not trivial.

gas in minor coal seams and adjacent shales should not be ignored when evaluating the producible gas in coal gas reservoirs, and that the gas in these formations may be produced earlier than gas in the main coal seam.
